# Decision: per-runner selection and policy

**Runner A** (bundled 1.21.3, `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, main module `go 1.21.0` + `toolchain go1.21.9`): `auto` = `local+auto`. Selection consults the toolchain line first; since go1.21.9 is newer than the default (bundled 1.21.3), the go command searches PATH for a program named `go1.21.9`; not found, it downloads and verifies the `golang.org/toolchain` module (v0.0.1-go1.21.9.GOOS-GOARCH) and runs it. Build succeeds, but requires network to the module path/proxy and checksum-DB access, so 1.21.9 is only run because it was downloaded as a module. (https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#select, https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download)

**Runner B** (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, module with `go 1.21.9`): `local` always runs the bundled 1.21.3. Since Go 1.21 the `go` line is a mandatory minimum; a toolchain refuses to use a module declaring a newer go line. So Runner B **refuses** with an error before building — the fix is network/toolchain access or pinning `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.9` with it downloaded. (https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#config)

**Runner C** (`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path`, same go.mod): default 1.21.3, still consults toolchain/go lines; 1.21.9 is newer, so it looks along PATH for `go1.21.9` and, finding none, the `+path` form disables the download fallback. It **stops and refuses** (runs in the module requiring 1.21.9). It skips startup switching; guarantee ends at "no downloads attempted."

**go vs. toolchain directives**
- `go`: mandatory minimum required Go version to use the module (as main module or a dependency); also sets enforced language version; main module's go line must be ≥ every dependency's go line (https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#go-notes; https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#config).
- `toolchain`: a *suggestion* of preferred toolchain; applies only when this module is the main module and default toolchain is older than it (https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#toolchain).

**Dependency suggestions vs. consumers**: a dependency's `toolchain` line has no direct effect on consumers during *startup* selection — only the main module's/go.work's go and toolchain lines matter. Its `go` line does propagate: `go get`/`go mod tidy` bump the main module's go line to ≥ each dependency's go line, and when a session acquires a module requiring a newer Go, `go get` may switch toolchains and rewrite the main module's toolchain line to record its own name (https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#switch).

**GOSUMDB=off proposal**: counterproductive and contrary to docs — toolchain downloads need checksums checked; "toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off" (https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download). It does not enable downloads; it breaks them. +path also does not make builds network-free — module dependency fetches use GOPROXY regardless, and proxy + checksum DB are the documented route for verifying the toolchain download. Correct CI approach: `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` with a reachable GOPROXY/proxy.golang.org and checksum DB, or pre-prime GOMODCACHE with the required version; `+path` only if toolchains are vendored onto PATH.

**Guarantees these settings do NOT establish** — and what would verify them: nothing is documented guaranteeing *reproducibility* (same runner can download different patch releases; verify via recorded toolchain output like a summary of `go version` per run) or fully deterministic network behavior under `auto` (ROM/non-doc claim UNVERIFIED by a narrower, doc-sourced experiment — e.g., confirming refusal text offline with a runner snapshot).# Decision: per-runner selection and policy

**Runner A** (bundled 1.21.3, `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, main module `go 1.21.0` + `toolchain go1.21.9`): `auto` is shorthand for `local+auto`. Startup selection consults the toolchain line first; since go1.21.9 is newer than the default (the bundled 1.21.3), the go command searches PATH for `go1.21.9`; finding none, it downloads and verifies the `golang.org/toolchain` module (v0.0.1-go1.21.9.GOOS-GOARCH) and runs it. Build succeeds, but requires network access to the module proxy and checksum database. https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#select, https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download

**Runner B** (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, module saying `go 1.21.9`): `local` always runs the bundled 1.21.3. Since Go 1.21 the go line is a *mandatory* minimum; a toolchain refuses to use a module declaring a newer go version and reports an error and exits. So Runner B **refuses** before building — no downloads are attempted, even though network could fix it. https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#config, https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#select

**Runner C** (`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path`, same go.mod as A): default is 1.21.3, but `+path` still consults the toolchain/go lines; since 1.21.9 is newer, it searches PATH — not found — and `+path` disables the download fallback. It **refuses** (can't build a main module whose required toolchain isn't found on PATH), rather than staying on 1.21.3.

**`go` vs `toolchain` directives**
- `go`: the mandatory minimum required Go version to use the module; it also sets the enforced language version, and a main module's go line must be ≥ every required dependency's go line. https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#go-notes, https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#config
- `toolchain`: a *suggested* toolchain; only effective while this module is the main module and when the default toolchain is older than the suggestion. https://go.dev/doc/modules/gomod-ref#toolchain

A dependency's `toolchain` suggestion does **not** directly force downstream consumers to switch during startup selection — only the consumer's own main-module/go.work directives matter there. But a dependency's `go` line does propagate: `go get`/`go mod tidy` keep the main module's go line ≥ each required module's go line, and when `go get` pulls in a module requiring a newer Go it may switch toolchains and also bump the main module's `toolchain` line to record its own version. https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#switch, https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#get

**GOSUMDB=off (`+path` network-free claim)**: rejected on two counts. Documented fact: "toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off," and GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB do not apply to toolchain downloads (https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download) — so GOSUMDB=off does not enable auto downloads; it breaks them, while also disabling all module checksum verification. `+path` does not make the whole build network-free: plain module dependency fetches use GOPROXY/checksums regardless (https://go.dev/doc/toolchain#download). Correct restricted-CI policy: keep default verification (`GOSUMDB` on, `checksum` mode), pre-populate the module cache (`go mod download` / baked `GOMODCACHE`) and, where needed, put the required `go1.21.9` on PATH or pre-seed GOMODCACHE so `+path`/`local` work without network — rather than weakening checks.

**Non-guarantees**: none of `GOTOOLCHAIN=local/local+auto`, or a toolchain directive guarantees reproducible/identical toolchain selection across runners or guarantees that startup selection alone works when the local toolchain is older than the module/dependency needs. UNVERIFIED: whether the `+path` "list scanning" behavior (switch #select section) still attempts any network traffic beyond PATH scan — needs a doc page on `cmd/go`'s `+path` list source to resolve.
